text:
maria_cs: FYI — Acme Inc reported a regression after the weekend rollout. They say concise invoice summaries are now hallucinating numbers and sometimes returning a refusal. Internal evals on our benchmark suite all passed. Posting the customer's raw example below.

maria_cs: CUSTOMER PROMPT (raw)
```
Summarize the invoice below in 3 bullets:
Invoice ID: 12345
Items:
- Hosting: $100
- Support: $50
Total: $150
```

maria_cs: CUSTOMER EXPECTED:
- Hosting — $100
- Support — $50
- Total — $150

maria_cs: CUSTOMER ACTUAL:
`Sorry, I can't assist with financial summaries of invoices.`
(or sometimes returns a 2-bullet summary and drops the total)

olga_support: Do we have their `request_id`/times? Did they include headers or options (streaming, system prompt) in the ticket? :thinking_face:

maria_cs: They attached one request_id and a screenshot of the response. request_id: `req_0a9f7c` (from Acme support bundle). Region: us-west1. Model reported in response metadata: `redwood-model-2.0`

deploy-bot: rolled out `redwood-model-2.0` -> prod at 2026-03-15T03:12:22Z, rollout=100% (canary ended: 2026-03-15T02:40:00Z)

kevin_ml: I reproduced quickly with the same model tag + default params and I got the refusal text — interesting. Note: our internal eval harness strips control chars and normalizes spaces/punctuation before sending. Did we try the customer's raw bytes?

maria_cs: I uploaded the raw payload from the customer (they included a copy of their client request). It contains a hidden NBSP after the word "Items:" and also an extra trailing newline.

ian_research: NBSPs and Unicode whitespace can change tokenization boundaries and sometimes trigger a safety heuristic when combined with short system prompts. Our benchmark set doesn't include weird whitespace variants — that could explain why our automated evals passed.

jenn_prodops: Routing logs show Acme's requests hit the `model-2.0-qa` variant for their tenant due to a tenant-specific rollout policy (they're on dedicated routing). That variant has an extra, lightweight content-safety wrapper we enabled for a previous customer. Might be interacting with their prompt.

kevin_ml: Repro notes: when I run the exact raw bytes (no normalization) against a local 2.0 build with the safety wrapper enabled, I reproduce the refusal. When I normalize whitespace, model returns expected bullets. So this is a mismatch between customer raw input and our eval preprocessing.

olga_support: So root cause hypothesis = preprocessing differences between customer SDK/client and our eval harness + tenant-specific safety wrapper.

ian_research: Action plan: 1) CS to collect all request_ids + raw payloads from Acme (maria_cs). 2) Eng (kevin_ml) will run targeted evals using the customer's raw prompt set across variants: model-2.0, model-2.0-qa, and model-1.9. 3) Research to audit the safety wrapper for whitespace sensitivity. 4) Docs/SDK to clarify normalization behavior.

maria_cs: Action: I've asked Acme for a dump of the last 24h of `request_id`s and attached the raw request they used. Ticket created: CS-4821.

jenn_prodops: I'll add an observability filter to capture future inbound bytes for this tenant (so we can see raw, un-normalized payloads).

kevin_ml: Quick mitigation: we can either 1) disable the safety wrapper for Acme's tenant temporarily, or 2) add a preprocessing normalization layer at the router to match our evals. I prefer a conservative approach: disable wrapper for Acme after confirming no safety violations in their history.

olga_support: Acme is blocked in prod — they flagged this as P1. CS requests a temporary rollback to the pre-2.0 variant or disable the wrapper as an interim fix.

ian_research: I'll run a batch of the customer's 50 failing prompts through an internal regression harness (raw bytes, all variants) and post results by EOD. If we confirm the wrapper is the trigger, we'll propose a patch that makes the wrapper whitespace-robust.

kevin_ml: For traceability I'm opening ENG ticket: ENG-12987 (repro + fix). Assigning to me.

maria_cs: Thanks. CS updated Acme: we're investigating root cause, collecting their raw requests, and may do a temporary config change. I'll keep you posted. :thumbsup:

jenn_prodops: Logging a follow-up: we should add a small test to our canary checklist to include random unicode whitespace permutations in the eval suite.

maria_cs: Next steps for CS: collect any additional examples, confirm whether they always include NBSP or it's sporadic. Also ask if they're using any custom SDKs or proxies that may inject chars.

kevin_ml: I'll post repro logs and diff between normalized vs raw tokenization in ENG-12987 when done.

ian_research: EOD update will include a binary yes/no on whether we can reproduce 100% deterministically and a suggested mitigation path (wrapper patch vs normalization).

maria_cs: tagging for visibility: @kevin_ml @ian_research @jenn_prodops @olga_support.
